verses.text: The Israelites came together as one community before the LORD at Mizpah, from Dan to Beersheba and from Gilead.
The leaders of all Israel's tribes took their places in the assembly of God's people. There were four hundred thousand foot soldiers armed with swords.
The people of Benjamin heard that the Israelites had gone up to Mizpah. The Israelites asked, “Tell us how this terrible thing happened.”
The Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, answered, “My concubine and I came to Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.
The men of Gibeah came after me and surrounded the house at night. They meant to kill me. They raped my concubine, and she died.
I cut her body into pieces and sent them throughout the land Israel inherited, because these men did something vile and outrageous in Israel.
Now all of you are Israelites. Tell us here what you think we should do.”
The people rose together and said, “None of us will go back to our tents or return to our homes.
Here's what we'll do to Gibeah. We'll cast lots to determine who goes up against it.

We'll assign ten men out of every hundred, a hundred out of every thousand, and a thousand out of every ten thousand across Israel's tribes to get food for the people. Then the others can follow through at Gibeah in Benjamin for the outrage its people committed in Israel.”
So the Israelites gathered against the city, united as one.
Israel's tribes sent men throughout Benjamin to ask, “What is this evil that's happened among you?
Hand over the wicked men in Gibeah so we can put them to death and remove this evil from Israel.” But Benjamin refused to listen to their fellow Israelites.
The Benjaminites came together from their towns at Gibeah to fight against Israel.
That day the towns of Benjamin counted twenty-six thousand swordsmen, plus seven hundred chosen men from Gibeah.
Among these soldiers were seven hundred chosen left-handed men. Every one could sling a stone at a hair without missing.
Apart from Benjamin, Israel counted four hundred thousand men armed with swords, all ready for battle.
The Israelites went up to Bethel and asked God, “Which tribe should go up first to fight Benjamin?” The LORD answered, “Judah first.”
In the morning the Israelites got up and camped against Gibeah.
The men of Israel went out to fight Benjamin and took up their positions at Gibeah.
The Benjaminites came out of Gibeah and struck down twenty-two thousand Israelites that day.
Israel's men encouraged one another and formed their battle line again where they'd stood the first day.
They went up and wept before the LORD until evening. They asked, “Should we go back to fight our relatives from Benjamin?” The LORD answered, “Go up against them.”
On the second day the Israelites went out against Benjamin again.
Benjamin came out of Gibeah on the second day and struck down another eighteen thousand Israelites, all armed with swords.
Then all the Israelites went up to Bethel. They sat there weeping in the LORD's presence and fasted until evening. Then they brought burnt offerings and peace offerings before him.
The Israelites asked the LORD for guidance. God's ark of the covenant was there at the time,

and Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, served before it. They asked, “Should we go out again to fight our relatives from Benjamin, or should we stop?” The LORD answered, “Go up. Tomorrow I'll hand them over to you.”
Israel set ambushes around Gibeah.
On the third day the Israelites went up against Benjamin and lined up for battle at Gibeah, just as before.
Benjamin came out against them and was drawn away from the city. They started striking down Israelites as before, in the fields and on the roads to Bethel and Gibeah. They killed about thirty men.
The Benjaminites said, “We're beating them just like the first time.” But the Israelites had planned to retreat and draw them away from the city onto the roads.
Israel's main force regrouped at Baal Tamar. Israel's men in hiding also rushed out from Maareh Geba.
Ten thousand chosen men from across Israel came against Gibeah. The fighting was fierce, and the Benjaminites didn't realize disaster was about to hit them.
The LORD defeated Benjamin before Israel. That day the Israelites struck down twenty-five thousand one hundred men of Benjamin, all armed with swords.
Then the Benjaminites realized they'd been beaten. The men of Israel had given ground because they relied on the men they'd stationed outside Gibeah.
The men in hiding rushed into Gibeah, spread through the city, and put it to the sword.
Israel's men had agreed that a great cloud of smoke rising from the city would be the signal from the men in hiding.
When Israel's men fell back during the battle, Benjamin began striking them down and killed about thirty. The Benjaminites thought, “We're beating them just like in the first battle.”
Then a column of smoke began to rise. The Benjaminites looked back and saw the whole city going up in smoke.
Israel's men turned on them. The Benjaminites panicked when they saw that disaster had overtaken them.
They fled from Israel toward the wilderness, but the fighting followed close behind. The men coming out of the towns struck them down in the middle of it.
The Israelites surrounded Benjamin, chased them, and struck them down at their resting place as far as the area east of Gibeah.
Eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell, all able warriors.
The rest fled toward the Rock of Rimmon in the wilderness. Israel struck down five thousand on the roads and pursued them to Gidom, where they struck down two thousand more.
In all, twenty-five thousand swordsmen of Benjamin fell that day. Every one was a warrior.
Six hundred men escaped to the Rock of Rimmon in the wilderness and stayed there four months.
The Israelites turned back against Benjamin and put to the sword everyone they found in the city, along with the livestock. They set fire to every town they came across.
